facts.statement: Banji was an extinct oviraptorid dinosaur that lived about 66 million years ago in what is now China.
facts.quote: Banji is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived approximately 66 million years ago during the later part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now China.

facts.statement: Banji was a small, lightly built, bipedal ground-dwelling carnivore estimated to be 65 cm long when juvenile.
facts.quote: It was a small, lightly built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, that was an estimated 65 cm long, as a juvenile.

facts.statement: The fossil was donated to the Chinese Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology by an amateur collector who found it near Ganzhou in Jiangxi Province.
facts.quote: It was donated to the Chinese Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology by an amateur collector who recovered the fossil near the city of Ganzhou, in Jiangxi Province.

facts.statement: The genus contains only one known species, Banji long, which means "striped crest dragon" in Chinese.
facts.quote: It contains only one known species, Banji long (斑嵴 龍), named from the Chinese for "striped crest dragon".

facts.statement: Banji was first described by Xu Xing and Feng-Lu Han in 2010.
facts.quote: It was first described by Xu Xing and Feng-Lu Han in 2010.

facts.statement: Banji had a tall, crested skull similar to other oviraptorids.
facts.quote: Banji possessed a tall, crested skull like some other oviraptorids.

facts.statement: The sides of Banji's crest were uniquely adorned with vertical striations, and it had grooves on the top of its lower jaw.
facts.quote: Uniquely, the sides of the crest are adorned with a series of vertical striations, as well as grooves on the top of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Banji differed from other oviraptorids by having an unusually long nasal opening that extended nearly to the eye socket along the crest.
facts.quote: Banji also differs from other oviraptorids in having an unusually long nasal opening that followed the curve of the crest nearly to the eye socket.

facts.statement: According to Xu et al. (2013), Banji is distinguished by a crest formed of nasal bones and premaxillae with a stepped end, longitudinal grooves, oblique striations, an elongate external naris near the orbit, a deep fossa on the pterygoid, grooves on the dentary, and tubercles on the surangular.
facts.quote: According to Xu et al. (2013), Banji can be distinguished based on the following characteristics: the crest is formed by the nasal bones and the premaxillae; the crest has a step-wise caudal end and bears two longitudinal grooves and numerous oblique striations on its lateral surfaces; the presence of a caudally located, extremely elongate, external naris near the orbit; the dorsal surface of the palatal ramus of the pterygoid has a deep fossa; several longitudinal grooves are present along the caudal portion of the dorsal margin of the dentary; several tubercles are present along the lateral shelf at the dorsal margin of the surangular.

facts.statement: In 2024, Andrea Cau suggested that Banji might represent an immature individual of the contemporary Corythoraptor, potentially making it a senior synonym.
facts.quote: In 2024, Andrea Cau considered it likely that Banji represents an immature individual of the contemporary Corythoraptor, making it a senior synonym of that taxon.

facts.statement: Banji is classified in the order Saurischia, suborder Theropoda, and family Oviraptoridae.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia subordo: Theropoda familia: Oviraptoridae

facts.statement: Banji lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype of Banji consists of a single nearly complete skull and lower jaw.
rejected.quote: The holotype specimen, IVPP V 16896, consists of a single nearly complete skull and lower jaw.
